questions.stem: This monitor tracing and idealized waveform plot exhaled CO2 against time. What does the Phase III plateau of this waveform represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A period of apnea with no airflow

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alveolar gas sampled at the end of expiration

explanation.summary: On a capnogram, Phase III is the alveolar plateau; its endpoint (ETCO2) reflects alveolar CO2 and approximates arterial PaCO2. Rising ETCO2 indicates hypercapnia/hypoventilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: On a capnogram, Phase III is the alveolar plateau; its endpoint (ETCO2) reflects alveolar CO2 and approximates arterial PaCO2. Rising ETCO2 indicates hypercapnia/hypoventilation.

questions.stem: These two lung histology fields are compared: panel A shows relatively preserved fine alveolar architecture, while panel B shows abnormally enlarged airspaces with destroyed, rarefied septal walls. The change in panel B is the structural hallmark of which condition?

explanation.summary: Emphysema is defined by permanent enlargement of airspaces distal to the terminal bronchiole with destruction of alveolar walls and loss of surface area, reducing gas exchange and contributing to CO2 retention/hypercapnia in advanced COPD.
explanation.whyCorrect: Emphysema is defined by permanent enlargement of airspaces distal to the terminal bronchiole with destruction of alveolar walls and loss of surface area, reducing gas exchange and contributing to CO2 retention/hypercapnia in advanced COPD.

questions.stem: This figure contrasts peripheral chemoreceptors (carotid bodies) with central chemoreceptors in the medulla. What is the primary stimulus for the CENTRAL chemoreceptors?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased H+ in the CSF generated from CO2

choices.label: C
choices.text: A rise in blood glucose concentration

choices.label: D
choices.text: A fall in arterial oxygen tension

choices.label: E
choices.text: A drop in systemic blood pressure

explanation.summary: CO2 diffuses across the blood-brain barrier into CSF, forming carbonic acid that releases H+; central chemoreceptors detect this H+ rise. Peripheral chemoreceptors are the ones that respond mainly to low arterial O2.
explanation.whyCorrect: CO2 diffuses across the blood-brain barrier into CSF, forming carbonic acid that releases H+; central chemoreceptors detect this H+ rise. Peripheral chemoreceptors are the ones that respond mainly to low arterial O2.

questions.stem: In this diagram, deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle passes two adjacent alveolar units: unit A is ventilated (O2 uptake shown) while unit B is perfused but not ventilated, and the outflow to the left atrium is a mix of both. What abnormality does this schematic best illustrate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diffusion limitation across a thickened membrane

explanation.summary: One alveolus is perfused but poorly ventilated, so its blood stays deoxygenated and mixes with well-oxygenated blood from the normal unit, lowering the combined PaO2. This venous admixture from low V/Q units is the classic mechanism of hypoxemia in V/Q mismatch.
explanation.whyCorrect: One alveolus is perfused but poorly ventilated, so its blood stays deoxygenated and mixes with well-oxygenated blood from the normal unit, lowering the combined PaO2. This venous admixture from low V/Q units is the classic mechanism of hypoxemia in V/Q mismatch.
